newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss approve deportation treaty with Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Swiss approve deportation treaty with Yugoslavia.

text.p: The Swiss government approved a deportation treaty with rump Yugoslavia on Monday that allows Berne to send back more than 12,000 Yugoslavs turned down for political asylum, the justice ministry said.
"Belgrade commits itself in the treaty to take back its citizens who do not have residency rights in Switzerland," a ministry statement said.
The ministry said there were more than 12,000 Yugoslavs whose asylum petitions had been rejected but who could not be returned to Yugoslavia under restrictions imposed by Belgrade in November 1994.
It said the treaty's detailed contents would not be published until the accord was approved by the government of rump Yugoslavia, which consists of Serbia and Montenegro, and signed by both sides.

Deadlines for the refugees to leave Switzerland were repeatedly extended while Berne sought a way to send them home. The cabinet on Monday granted another extension, until August 31, to allow time for the treaty with Belgrade to take effect.

Berne recognised rump Yugoslavia and resumed diplomatic relations late last year after the European Union normalised ties following the 1995 Dayton peace agreement to end the war between former Yugoslav Croats, Serbs and Moslems.
